newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mixed, underpinned by wheat rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mixed, underpinned by wheat rally.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed, underpinned by a rally in wheat and by a bullish corn number in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn for the week ended April 10 totaled 671,000 tonnes, near the high end of expectations for 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Traders also said Wednesday's break in the market on "mad cow" rumors was overdone.

Corn dropped Wednesday on technical selling, better crop weather and a wire service story which stated an Indiana farmer died from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), an illness in humans similar to Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy in some animals, also called "mad cow" disease.
It was unknown how the farmer contracted CJD but traders Wednesday reasoned that a scare about U.S. beef could cut beef consumption and subsequently cut feed needs, especially corn.

However, the Indiana Health Department said it sees several cases of CJD a year. No cases of CJD in the U.S. have ever been linked to eating beef and there has never been a case of BSE reported in U.S. cattle.
Corn closed two cents higher to 1/4 lower, with May down 1/4 at $2.97. July was up 1/2 at $2.97-3/4.

Many traders cited Wednesday's break below the 40-day moving average (MA) in the July at roughly $3.00 per bushel as a chief bearish technical factor for the market. "They're headed to the 50-day moving averages now and probably won't stop until they get there," a trader said referring to the fund long liquidation that has been occurring in corn futures.
The 50-day MA for the July Thursday closed at $2.95-1/4.
"The market is still long, it's overbought and there probably will be more liquidation," said Paul Haugens of FIMAT Futures. "Consumers are fairly well covered."
In spread trading, Cargill Inc did 3.5 million July/May at even money and Merrill Lynch Futures spread 2.5 million May/July at even money, traders said.

Griffin Trading sold four million bushels of July, O'Connor and Co sold four million July and Refco Inc sold four million July and sold three million May, traders said. Refco also bought three million July and bought three million December, floor sources said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 78,000 contracts, below the 94,457 traded Wednesday.
In corn options, USA Trading sold 500 May $2.90 puts at 1/2 cent, Tenco Inc sold 400 May $3.00 puts at two cents and sold 200 July $2.80 puts at 5-7/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, below the 24,179 traded Wednesday.
